content: 1. Porta M. authored A Dictionary of Epidemiology, 5th edition, published by Oxford University Press in 2008. 2. Fleming TR and DeMets DL critically examined the use of surrogate endpoints in clinical trials, questioning their reliability in Annals of Internal Medicine, October 1996, volume 125, issue 7, pages 605-613. 3. Prentice RL defined and established operational criteria for surrogate endpoints in clinical trials in Statistics in Medicine, April 1989, volume 8, issue 4, pages 431-440. 4. Qin L, Gilbert PB, Corey L, McElrath MJ, and Self SG proposed a framework for evaluating immunological correlates of protection in vaccine trials in Journal of Infectious Diseases, November 2007, volume 196, issue 9, pages 1304-1312. 5. Chen RT et al. reassessed protective titers of measles antibodies in Journal of Infectious Diseases, November 1990, volume 162, issue 5, pages 1036-1042. 6. Naniche D explored the human immunological response to measles virus infection in Current Topics in Microbiology and Immunology, 2009, volume 330, pages 151-171. 7. Sterne JAC et al. investigated whether the size of Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) scars correlates with protection against tuberculosis or leprosy in Tubercle and Lung Disease, 1996, volume 77, pages 117-123. 8. Kester KE et al. conducted a randomized, double-blind, phase 2a trial on malaria-naive adults to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and immunological correlates of protection of RTS,S/AS01B and RTS,S/AS02A falciparum malaria vaccines in Journal of Infectious Diseases, 2009, volume 200, pages 337-346. 9. Greenland S, Pearl J, and Robins JM discussed the use of causal diagrams in epidemiologic research in Epidemiology, 1999, volume 10, pages 37-48. 10. Edelman R et al. conducted a phase II study on the safety and immunogenicity of type F botulinum toxoid in adult volunteers, published in Vaccine, 2003, volume 21, pages 4335-4347. 11. Wassilak SGF et al. reviewed tetanus toxoid in the 5th edition of Vaccines, edited by Plotkin SA, Orenstein WA, and Offit P, published by Saunders Elsevier in 2008. 12. Franco MA, Angel J, and Greenberg HB examined immunity and correlates of protection for rotavirus vaccines in Vaccine, April 2006, volume 24, issue 15, pages 2718-2731. 13. Schneerson R et al. quantitatively measured natural and immunization-induced Haemophilus influenzae type b capsular polysaccharide antibodies in Pediatric Research. 14. D’Arcy Hart P et al. studied the immunity conferred by BCG and vole bacillus vaccines in relation to tuberculin sensitivity and vaccine variations in Tubercle (London), 1967, volume 48, pages 201-210. 15. Saaka M et al. evaluated the immunogenicity and serotype-specific efficacy of a 9-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV-9) during a trial in The Gambia, published in Vaccine, July 2008, volume 26, issues 29-30, pages 3719-3726. 16. Miller E et al. documented the planning, registration, and implementation of a meningococcal serogroup C immunization campaign in the UK in Vaccine, 2002, volume 20, Supplement 1, pages S58-S67. 17. Borrow R et al. reevaluated the serological basis for using meningococcal serogroup C conjugate vaccines in the UK in Infection and Immunity, 2001, volume 69, issue 3, pages 1568-1573. 18. Goldschneider I et al. studied human immunity to meningococcus, focusing on the role of humoral antibodies in Journal of Experimental Medicine, June 1969, volume 129, issue 6, pages 1307-1326. 19. Gill HK et al. investigated delayed-type hypersensitivity in volunteers immunized with a candidate leprosy vaccine in Bulletin of the World Health Organization, 1986, volume 64, pages 121-126. 20. Fine PEM et al. explored delayed-type hypersensitivity, mycobacterial vaccines, and protective immunity in The Lancet, 1994, volume 344, issue 8932, pages 1245-1249. 21. The Karonga Prevention Trial Group conducted a randomized controlled trial on BCG and Mycobacterium leprae vaccines for leprosy and tuberculosis prevention in Malawi, published in The Lancet, 1996, volume 348, pages 17-24. 22. Santosham M et al. studied the prevention of Haemophilus influenzae type b infections in high-risk infants treated with bacterial polysaccharide immune globulin in New England Journal of Medicine, October 1987, volume 317, issue 15, pages 923-929. 23. O’Reilly RJ et al. correlated circulating polyribophosphate levels with clinical outcomes and antibody responses in Haemophilus influenzae type b meningitis in Journal of Clinical Investigation, October 1975, volume 56, issue 4, pages 1012-1022. 24. Tacket CO et al. conducted a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial on the efficacy of a live oral cholera vaccine in preventing cholera in Infection and Immunity, December 1999, volume 67, issue 12, pages 6341-6345. 25. Jack AD et al. determined protective levels of hepatitis B antibodies in Journal of Infectious Diseases, February 1999, volume 179, issue 2, pages 489-492. 26. Ndumbe PM et al. compared natural and artificial immunity to varicella-zoster virus in Journal of Medical Virology, 1988, volume 25, issue 2, pages 171-179. 27. Horwitz O et al. analyzed the epidemiology and natural history of measles in Denmark in American Journal of Epidemiology, August 1974, volume 100, issue 2, pages 136-149. 28. Van Rie A et al. examined the role of maternal pertussis antibodies in infants in Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal, May 2005, volume 24, Supplement 5, pages S62-S65. 29. A collaborative study by the Kenyan Ministry of Health and WHO assessed measles immunity in the first year of life and the optimal age for vaccination in Kenyan children, published in Bulletin of the World Health Organization, 1977, volume 55, pages 21-31. 30. Glass RI et al. demonstrated protection against cholera in breastfed children through antibodies in breast milk in New England Journal of Medicine, June 1983, volume 308, issue 23, pages 1389-1392.
